title: Orchestrated bridge recommendation for customer POC
body:
Purpose
-----
Notes and recommendation for a small-to-medium customer POC that needs low friction onboarding but may migrate between hosted -> dedicated -> private hosting within 3–12 months. This doc captures a pragmatic, minimal-risk bridge architecture ("orchestrated bridge") and an actionable runbook for the first 6 weeks.

Audience
--------
Solutions Engineers, Customer Platform Engineers, Customer SREs, Sales Engineer.

Summary recommendation (one-liner)
--------------------------------
Start the customer on a hosted instance with a lightweight orchestrator shim that records routing policy and preserves request/response metadata, enabling transparent migration to a dedicated pool or private control plane without changing the application contract.

Why this approach
------------------
- Fast time-to-value: hosted reduces procurement friction and provides immediate telemetry.
- Migration hygiene: the orchestrator shim abstracts routing, auth, and metrics so model endpoints can change behind a stable API key and client config.
- Cost visibility: telemetry captures per-request latency/token cost which informs when to migrate to Dedicated.
- Regulatory flexibility: the shim can enforce data-path tagging to decide whether a request needs private handling.

High-level architecture (conceptual)
-----------------------------------
1) Customer app -> Redwood API (hosted) : default path for initial weeks.
2) Orchestrator shim (deployed as lightweight sidecar or gateway rule on the customer's ingress) : records request fingerprint, tenant tag, and routing preference; can signal a config service to route to Dedicated/Private when needed.
3) Dedicated pool / Private control plane: pre-provisioned (warm) based on forecast signals from telemetry.
4) Fallback policy: if Dedicated is saturated, orchestrator falls back to hosted model (with anonymization) per policy.

Key design elements (details)
---------------------------
- Identity and auth: use customer API key mapped to Redwood tenant. Shim should not store raw PII; use tokenization for sample traces.
- Data path tagging: requests include a header X-RW-DATA-CLASS with values {public, sensitive} to select host. Default public -> hosted. Sensitive -> private/dedicated.
- Audit logs: centralize audit events to the customer's SIEM (via S3/Kinesis endpoint) for Private deployments.
- KMS: for Private mode, integrate with customer KMS (customer-managed CMK) for encryption-at-rest of KV caches and logs.
- SR/QA: small e2e test harness (postman collection + load profile) included in repo for customer engineers.

Proof-of-concept runbook (6 weeks)
----------------------------------
Week 0: Prep (2–3 days)
- Provision hosted API credentials and create a tenant in staging.
- Share quickstart sample app and sidecar container image.
- Agree success criteria with customer: latency < 300ms p95 for short prompts, model quality threshold (BLEU/ROUGE or business metric), and cost target.

Week 1: Integration (1 week)
- Customer integrates SDK or direct REST to hosted endpoint.
- Deploy orchestrator shim in front of API calls; collect initial telemetry.
- Run baseline functional tests.

Week 2–3: Load/Cost observations (2 weeks)
- Execute representative traffic (synthetic + small real sample) to capture token distribution, sequence lengths, and latency distribution.
- Identify common prefixes for caching opportunities.

Week 4–5: Dedicated warmup (1–2 weeks)
- If 3-day rolling average cost or latency exceed thresholds, provision a small Dedicated slice (2 x A100-equivalent vGPUs or equivalent quantized instances depending on model).
- Configure orchestrator routing rule to send 10% canary traffic to Dedicated.
- Validate model parity and run regression prompts.

Week 6: Canary ramp and decision
- Ramp to 50% traffic if parity is good and cost delta meets expectations.
- Customer sign-off point: production rollout / continue on hosted for longer.

Operational controls and telemetry
---------------------------------
- Instrumentation: per-request metadata (tenant_id, prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, model_id, route, latency_ms, error_code).
- Dashboards: per-tenant token burn, p50/p95 latency, per-route error rate, model regression alerts tied to guardset (10–20 golden prompts).
- Alerts: auto alert when Dedicated pool saturates > 80% for 5m or when hosted p95 latency increases > 2x baseline.

Fallback policies and safety nets
--------------------------------
- Soft fallback: when Dedicated overloaded, 50% of failed requests be retried to hosted with response anonymization flag.
- Graceful degradation: for sensitive data tagged requests, if Private is down, buffer and return 503 with retry guidance (do not auto-failover to hosted unless customer explicitly permits).

Networking and compliance considerations
--------------------------------------
- For Private deployments we require a VPN or PrivateLink + restrictive egress rules. Document the customer's firewall rules and proxies in the kickoff.
- Data residency: orchestrator must log region_tag for each request; routing policy can enforce region constraint.

Cost and capacity heuristics (back-of-envelope)
----------------------------------------------
- Small POC: hosted costs only — expect $1k–$5k/month depending on usage (10k–100k tokens/day).
- Dedicated minimal warm slice: ~$15k–$25k/month (reserved) for predictable throughput (depends on GPU type).
- Migration trigger examples: sustained >25% higher cost vs hosted OR p95 latency < dedicated by >50ms while cost per token improves >15%.

Open questions & risk log (work-in-progress)
-------------------------------------------
- How many golden prompts do customers want to check for parity? Recommend 12–20 mixing short/long prompts.
- Telemetry privacy: what exact token-level traces are acceptable for customer observability vs privacy constraints?
- KMS onboarding lead time: typically 2–3 weeks if customer requires HSM-backed keys.

Action items (who/when)
-----------------------
- Aisha: finalize sidecar container and quickstart repo (by 2024-10-25).
- Marco: add preset routing templates for "sensitive->private" and "latency-first->dedicated" to SE repo (by 2024-10-28).
- Priya: prepare canary checklist and regression guardset template (by 2024-11-01).
- Customer SW: provide expected QPS and sample prompts for golden set (by kickoff).

Appendix: quick checklist for kickoff call
-----------------------------------------
- Confirm success criteria and escalation path.
- Confirm KMS and logging requirements.
- Agree canary percentage and rollback triggers.
- Schedule weekly sync for first 6 weeks.

Notes to self
------------
- Keep the initial default conservative: prefer hosted for public data, private only when contract/security requires it.
- This pattern reduces churn on client SDKs and avoids re-issuing keys when migrations occur.
- Follow up: add a prescriptive terraform snippet for shim enablement in next iteration.
